name: Electronic digital computer
definition: A programmable electronic machine that stores data and runs programs to calculate and process information far faster than people.

first_pass.what: ENIAC ran its first real program (Los Alamos problem, likely thermonuclear calculations) at the Moore School, University of Pennsylvania

first_pass_note: No wikidata URL seen. Public ENIAC unveiling Feb 1946 not searched.

name: Analog computer
definition: A machine that solves equations by modelling them with continuous mechanical or electrical quantities, such as a differential analyzer.

first_pass.what: Vannevar Bush and colleagues at MIT completed the operational mechanical Differential Analyzer

name: Punched-card data processing
definition: Tabulating and sorting machines that read records coded as holes in cards or tape to count, sort and account.

first_pass.what: Herman Hollerith's punched-card tabulating machines used to tabulate the 1890 US Census

first_pass_note: 1888 Baltimore health trial not verified; 1890 census chosen.

name: Programmed machine control by tape or program
definition: Machines whose actions are driven by a recorded sequence of instructions on tape, cards or memory rather than by an operator.

first_pass.what: MIT demonstrated a Cincinnati Hydrotel milling machine driven by pre-punched tape (numerical control), for Parsons Corporation/US Air Force

first_pass_note: Jacquard loom (1804) is an earlier tape/card-driven machine but was not verified by search; 1952 NC demo only.

name: Integrated circuit and microminiaturized electronics
definition: Electronic circuits made as tiny solid-state components, such as transistors and microchips, packed into very small spaces.

first_pass.what: Jack Kilby demonstrated the first working integrated circuit (germanium) to managers at Texas Instruments, Dallas

name: Cryotron or superconducting computer
definition: A computer built from switching elements that work by superconductivity at liquid-helium temperatures.
first_pass_note: Buck's cryotron (1953-55) was a single superconducting switching element; no working cryotron computer confirmed in searches, so no milestones given.

name: Magnetic tape, drum and disk storage
definition: Recording machine data or sound on magnetized tape, wire, drums or disks for later retrieval.

first_pass.what: IBM announced the 305 RAMAC with the 350 disk storage unit, first commercial moving-head magnetic disk system, with units already installed at the US Navy and companies

first_pass_note: Poulsen 1898 and UNIVAC tape 1951 not verified by search; RAMAC only.

name: Microfilm and compact document storage
definition: Storing books and records as miniaturized photographic images on film, spools or cards that are read through a viewer.

first_pass.what: John Benjamin Dancer in England made the first microphotographs (documents reduced to microscopic size)
Eastman Kodak bought George McCarthy's Checkograph and marketed it as Recordak, microfilming bank checks

first_pass_note: Dancer 1839 microphotography is a loose fit to film-storage-with-viewer; Recordak 1928 is the first commercial use.

name: Artificial neural network
definition: A computer built or programmed as many interconnected neuron-like units that together compute and learn, modelled on the brain.

first_pass.what: Frank Rosenblatt's Perceptron (Cornell Aeronautical Lab, Navy-funded) demonstrated learning; 1958 Navy press event (IBM 704 simulation, Mark I hardware followed; sources disagree on exact public demo date, 1958 vs 1960)

first_pass_note: Date of public Mark I demo disputed (1958 vs 1960).

name: Biological computer
definition: A computing system built from living cells, organic chemistry or brain tissue instead of electronics.

first_pass.what: Leonard Adleman solved a seven-node Hamiltonian path problem with DNA molecules in the lab (Science, Nov 1994)

first_pass_note: Only laboratory demonstrations; no practical use.

name: Pocket electronic calculator
definition: A small battery-powered electronic device that performs arithmetic for one person on demand.

first_pass.what: Bowmar 901B, early pocket-size LED electronic calculator built on a TI chip, sold to consumers (introduction year 1971 vs 1972 disputed)

first_pass_note: Bowmar 901B date uncertain (1971/1972); HP-35 1972 and TI Cal-Tech 1967 are alternate candidates.

name: Personal computer
definition: A computer small and cheap enough for an individual to own and use at home or at a desk.

first_pass.what: MITS Altair 8800 kit computer on the cover of Popular Electronics, sold to individuals (about 2,000 in first month)
Apple II, Commodore PET and TRS-80 launched as ready-to-use home computers sold to the public

first_pass_note: Altair 8800 chosen as first practical use; 1977 trinity as mass adoption.

name: Wearable computer and personal digital assistant
definition: A small body-worn or pocket electronic device that stores notes, schedules and reminders and gives its owner information on demand.

first_pass.what: Psion Organiser, handheld pocket computer with diary/database, launched in the UK (Organiser II 1986 is often called the first usable PDA)
Palm Computing's PalmPilot, introduced March 1996, made PDAs a consumer must-have

first_pass_note: Organiser vs Organiser II (1986) dating disputed.

name: Scientific supercomputing
definition: Very fast computers used to solve large mathematical and scientific problems beyond human calculation.

first_pass.what: CDC 6600 (Seymour Cray, released 1964), generally considered the first successful supercomputer, delivered to Livermore and Los Alamos; Manchester Atlas (Dec 1962) is an earlier contender

first_pass_note: Atlas 1962 and IBM 7030 are contenders; 'first supercomputer' contested.

name: Computer simulation and modelling
definition: Running a mathematical model of a physical, military or social system on a computer to see how it would behave.

first_pass.what: ENIAC ran the first computerized Monte Carlo simulations, of neutron diffusion in fission weapons, for Los Alamos (March-May 1948)

first_pass_note: No milestone confirmed by search (ENIAC Monte Carlo 1948 / SAGE not verified), so none given.
